chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Demonstrating the Pretty Foot and Get on the Good Foot
summary: Green links the Pretty Foot to the cakewalk and demonstrates it and the polka-style Get on the Good Foot.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: It could be a contest dance, you see. (Recording interruption) The Cake Walk, Chuck, would be a sort of Pretty Foot.
That's it. That's the number one in Chocolate Dandy, the world, the Cake Walk, (unintelligible) Walter Bailey, (Geatty), see. (Recording interruption)
I would really love to see the Pretty Foot, Chuck, if you can do it for us.
Okay. This should really be something good.
I'm looking forward to it too.
Then, if it was a polka they would go into Get on the Good Foot, you know, that's polka.
Like that. That's Get on the Good Foot.

I think, George, we can both understand why they call it the Pretty Foot, because I'm sure you noticed how pretty that did look and most of the work seemed to be on the toes. Very nimble. (Recording interruption) I'm so sorry.
Well, as I said, it was mostly on the toes and I can understand it -- why they call it the Pretty Foot because it is very, very pretty. It's light and
pretty, and all the work is mostly on the toes.
Lovely for a girl. I can't wait to do it.
